title: PACE%2BCode%2BD%2B2023.pdf — section 111
text:
4. The eye-witness shall be shown not less than twelve photographs at a time, which shall, as
far as possible, all be of a similar type.

5. When the eye-witness is shown the photographs, they shall be told the photograph of the
person they saw on a specified earlier occasion may, or may not, be amongst them and if
they cannot make an identification, they should say so. The eye-witness shall also be told
they should not make a decision until they have viewed at least twelve photographs. The
eye-witness shall not be prompted or guided in any way but shall be left to make any
selection without help.

6. If an eye-witness makes an identification from photographs, unless the person identified is
otherwise eliminated from enquiries or is not available, other eye- witnesses shall not be
shown photographs. But both they, and the eye- witness who has made the identification,
shall be asked to attend a video identification, an identification parade or group identification
unless there is no dispute about the suspect’s identification.
